trigger_model.why_a_single_request_is_accidentally_saf: align mode skips null blocks, so the defect needs mixed-length requests over a shared prefix; the probe drives that condition deliberately rather than hoping for it
construction: One ASCII English document per experiment. Every request is a nested token prefix of it, so all requests share a token-identical prefix and a later, longer request's prefix hit reaches blocks published by an earlier, shorter one.

Ten document prefix lengths, none a multiple of the 1600-token mamba block: 3000, 4100, 5300, 6500, 7700, 8200, 9900, 11000, 12300, 15400. With the 35-token chat head and the question tail the ten prompt lengths are 3141, 4241, 5441, 6641, 7841, 8341, 10041, 11141, 12441, 15541 and their residues mod 1600 are 1541, 641, 1041, 1441, 241, 441, 341, 1241, 1541, 1141 - no prompt is block aligned.
--max-num-batched-tokens 2048 puts chunk ends at multiples of 2048; between 1 and 7 chunk ends per request land mid-block, which is exactly the window the vendored guard fails to align.

Three passes of thirty requests total: pass 1 interleaved short/long/shorter/longer, pass 2 the same order replayed against a warm cache, pass 3 ascending as a persistence check, because a poisoned entry survives until process restart.
Sampling is greedy: temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 0, max_tokens 220, OpenAI-compatible /v1/completions with explicit token ids.

Fourth pass, boundary-straddle: four pairs whose shared prefixes are 2900/3500, 4500/5100, 6100/6700 and 7700/8300 tokens. The first of each pair ends 300 tokens short of a 1600-token block boundary; the second crosses exactly that boundary and can only get there through the entry the first one published. 38 requests in total.
trigger_model.ground_truth_per_request: two planted needle codes that must be retrieved verbatim (one shallow, always inside the shortest prefix; one as deep as the request's own prefix allows), one arithmetic answer, and a 40-60 word English summary that gives the corruption detector material. 16 needles are planted at measured token depths 891 through 12722.

threshold_notes.out_of_script_fraction_gt: fraction of response characters outside the expected script set (ASCII printable plus a short list of English typographic characters). Prompt, document and answer format are pure ASCII English, so appreciable non-ASCII mass is the reported multilingual token soup. 2 % of a ~600 character answer is ~12 characters, well above an occasional curly quote.
threshold_notes.replacement_char_count_ge: U+FFFD in the decoded response. The reporter names replacement characters explicitly; one is already a defect.
threshold_notes.longest_repeated_block_chars_ge: longest substring occurring at least twice in the response, overlaps allowed. The reporter names repeated blocks. 80 characters is far longer than the answer scaffold and longer than any phrase a 60-word summary repeats by chance.
threshold_notes.ngram5_repetition_ratio_ge: 1 - unique_5grams / total_5grams over whitespace-split words, computed only at 30 words or more. Catches degenerate looping that does not produce one single long verbatim block.
threshold_notes.answer_noise_band_requests: how many differing requests out of the thirty are tolerated when asking whether the patched arm matches the prefix-caching-off arm. Greedy decoding is deterministic per state, but cached and uncached paths take different kernel routes, so one differing request out of thirty is treated as probe noise.

pre_registration.a_request_fails_if: the corruption detector fires on its response, or any SCORED checkable answer is wrong. The scored answers are A1 and A2 (the two planted needle codes) and A3 (the record numbers of the two needle records). A4, the arithmetic item, is asked, parsed and reported on every row but is not scored; see amendment_1.

verdict_rules.reproduced: arm A has at least one failing request AND arm B has none on the identical prompt set
verdict_rules.partially_reproduced: neither arm is clean but arm A fails at least three more requests than arm B; recorded as degradation, not as the reported defect
verdict_rules.not_reproduced: arm A has no failing request. This is a publishable negative and will be published as one: it would mean the reporter's trigger needs something this probe did not model, most plausibly LMCache 0.5.2's kv_both disk reuse path, which restores state from outside vLLM's own prefix cache and is named here in advance as the next experiment.
verdict_rules.fixed: arm A reproduced AND arm C has zero corrupted requests AND arm C fails at most one more request than arm B
verdict_rules.fix_not_exercised: arm A did not reproduce, so a clean arm C cannot be read as the fix working
verdict_rules.arm_d_reporting: arm D is reported on its own row and is never folded into the arm C verdict, so the two absent upstream fixes are never conflated
verdict_rules.arm_e_is_not_part_of_the_correctness_ver: arm E measures prefix-reuse economics only; it can neither create nor rescue a correctness verdict
verdict_rules.secondary_concurrency_pair: arms A2 and B2 repeat A and B at --max-num-seqs 4. If A2 has at least one failing request and B2 has none, the verdict is reproduced_with_concurrency_deviation and the deviation is named in every statement of it. A2/B2 cannot make the primary A/B verdict positive.

what_changed: The arithmetic item was a two-digit multiplication plus a three-digit addend and is no longer scored; it is replaced in the pass/fail rule by a third retrieval item (A3, the record numbers of the two needle records) and demoted to a reported diagnostic (A4, now a two-digit addition).

Added a fourth prompt pass, boundary-straddle: four pairs whose shared prefixes are 2900/3500, 4500/5100, 6100/6700 and 7700/8300 tokens, so the first request of each pair ends 300 tokens short of a 1600-token block boundary and the second crosses exactly that boundary. 30 requests became 38.

Added logprobs=1 to every request. Greedy sampling plus identical prompts makes the emitted token ids and their chosen-token logprobs directly comparable across arms, so every arm is additionally compared against arm B by identical-token count and by mean and maximum absolute chosen-logprob delta. This is the instrument upstream used to measure PR #51812 and it detects state divergence even when the argmax never changes.

Added arms A2 and B2 at --max-num-seqs 4 (the reporter runs 1). A batch of one never forms the mixed batch that upstream says PR #51812 needs, and concurrency is the most plausible amplifier the original design did not model.
Fixed the SpecDecoding log regex, which had been written against a format this build does not emit and matched zero windows.
amendment_1.why: A pilot run of arm A on the original prompt set, published in full at receipts/apc-repro-raw/pilot/, failed 22 of 30 requests. Every one of those failures was the arithmetic item, and nothing else: needle retrieval was 30/30 on A1 and 30/30 on A2, the corruption detector never fired on any request, the longest repeated block over the whole run was 13 characters against a threshold of 80, and the 5-gram repetition ratio was 0.0 throughout. The arithmetic item was therefore measuring this model's mental arithmetic, not the integrity of its recurrent state, and scoring it would have drowned the signal the probe exists to find. The errors were near misses of exactly the kind a language model makes on multi-digit multiplication (2472 answered as 2482, 2546 as 2566, 1809 as 1789).
amendment_1.what_did_not_change: Every corruption threshold above is untouched, and no threshold was moved after seeing any data. The pilot is published rather than discarded, including its 30 full responses.
amendment_1.pilot_artifacts: receipts/apc-repro-raw/pilot/ (arm-A.json with all 30 rows, server-A.log, command-A.json, startup-facts-A.txt, gpu-A.csv)
amendment_1.pilot_confirmed_the_condition_was_real: the pilot server log records 'mamba_cache_mode': 'align' and enable_prefix_caching=True in the engine configuration, the banner warning that prefix caching in align mode is experimental, a measured mamba/attention block size of 1600 tokens, a GPU KV cache of 223,677 tokens, and a final prefix cache hit rate of 63.6 %. The reporter's condition was genuinely in effect and the cache was genuinely being hit.

arms.B: release image, --no-enable-prefix-caching (the condition every published measurement ran in)

deviations_from_the_reporter_and_why: --quantization exl3 with this edition's mxfp8 quantization-config ignore list: required for the model to load at all.
the edition's own chat template with enable_thinking=false, not the reporter's custom template: his template is not published and a reasoning preamble would spend the answer budget.

interpretation.the_condition_was_genuinely_in_effect: Arm A's engine configuration line records 'enable_prefix_caching': True and 'mamba_cache_mode': 'align', the banner warns that prefix caching in align mode is experimental, the measured mamba and attention block size is 1600 tokens, the KV cache is 223,677 tokens, and the run finished at a 62.9 % prefix cache hit rate. divergence_measurement.why_it_matters: Identical greedy prompts make every emitted token comparable across arms, so this detects state divergence far below the level that produces visible corruption. It is the instrument upstream used to measure PR #51812.
divergence_measurement.noise_floor: Arm Bn is arm B repeated on a second fresh server with byte-identical flags. Against arm B it reproduced only 20 of 38 responses token-for-token and carried a mean absolute chosen-logprob difference of 0.0823. That is this build's run-to-run floor with nothing changed at all, and every other number has to be read against it.
divergence_measurement.reading: Turning prefix caching on moves the chosen-token logprobs about 29 % more than a bit-identical rerun does, and never enough to change an answer. Turning concurrency on without prefix caching moves them exactly as much as a rerun does. Crucially the patched arm C sits at 1.28x, indistinguishable from the unpatched arm A at 1.29x, so the residual drift is the ordinary numerical difference between a recomputed and a restored prefix, not the #51113 defect. This is a bound, not an absence: it says the defect did not perturb this workload measurably, not that it cannot perturb any workload.
divergence_measurement.honest_caveat: The floor itself is large. Only 53 % of responses reproduce token-for-token across two identical servers, so this build is not bit-reproducible run to run and small divergences cannot be attributed to any single cause.

why_it_may_not_have_reproduced: LMCache is absent. The reporter runs LMCache 0.5.2 in kv_both disk mode with chunk 1600, a second, independent state-restore path layered on top of vLLM's prefix cache, with its own chunking and its own notion of what a reusable prefix is. This probe exercises only vLLM's own cache. This is the single largest untested difference and it is the named next experiment.
His chat template is not published and is not the one used here; a template that changes the token stream changes exactly which prefixes are shared and where chunk ends land.

His workload is multi-turn conversational with a growing prefix and, from the symptom description, likely multimodal at least some of the time. This probe is single-turn, text only, with nested prefixes of a synthetic document.

Blast radius may simply be narrower than the source reading suggests: the exposed window is (P mod 1600) + 1600 tokens of GDN recurrent state, and this model's needle retrieval leans on its full-attention layers, whose KV is cached correctly either way. A truncated recurrent state can therefore degrade fluency long before it breaks retrieval, and this probe scores retrieval.
interpretation.next_experiment: Reproduce with LMCache 0.5.2 in the loop: same image, same flags, plus kv_both disk mode at chunk 1600, multi-turn with a growing prefix, and the reporter's own template if he will share it. If that reproduces, the fix ordering question becomes whether #51113 alone is sufficient. If it does not, the next suspect is his template plus multimodal input rather than either upstream patch.

settled: PR #51113 is absent from the release digest and present in the superset digest, verified by sha256 inside both images before any measurement.

Running the reporter's condition on our published context edition for 38 requests over deliberately mid-block prefixes produces no corruption, no wrong answers and no acceptance collapse on this hardware.
The patched superset image is not worse than the release image on any measured axis: same zero failures, same acceptance band, same divergence from the no-cache control within noise.
Prefix caching is a very large performance lever on this model and is safe on the patched image over this workload.
not_settled: Whether PR #51113 is the cause of the reporter's symptoms. It is not shown to be, and it is not shown not to be.
Whether LMCache's reuse path triggers it. Not tested at all.
Whether PR #51812 fixes anything here. At --max-num-seqs 1 there is no mixed batch, which upstream says is the only condition it bites in, so arm D shows only that the module is harmless.
Whether prefix caching is safe on the unpatched release image in general. Arm A was clean over this workload, but the source defect is real and the safe recommendation is unchanged.
